chunks: A number of our companions, from among our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not correct for the girl when she menstruates unless she wears a scarf, unless she does not find it.

key_terms.إِلَّا أَنْ لَا تَجِدَهُ: Unless she does not find it (condition of inability)

ai.seo_question: When does a girl become obligated to wear a headscarf in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the obligation of the khimar for a young girl is triggered by the onset of menstruation, marking her transition to legal maturity (bulugh). The hadith introduces the principle of 'al-ghina' (ability/capacity) as a condition for this specific obligation, noting that if she lacks the means to acquire a scarf, the duty is lifted, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease and practicality in religious obligations.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
It is not correct for the girl when she menstruates unless she wears a scarf, unless she does not find it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not proper for a girl who experiences Hayd (menses) not to use a veil except if she does not experience it.’”
